conviction_note: The findings roughly cancel, sum -0.1. Management has said Q3 cost trend held, and the CFO publicly gave 2027 margin targets (positive). Against that, the $4.12 Q3 bar sits about $0.8 above the cadence implied by the company's own guide ('slightly more in 3Q than 4Q' on an H2 of $5.89-6.39), and the last beat-and-raise faded from +7.3% pre-market to +1.16% at the close. The scaled number is p_up 53 on abs 7.0, so +0.42. It is small and positive because the lean agrees with an upside-paid skew (-7.2) and is therefore partly priced. The gap between the two measurements is that the positive facts are public and company-level, while the negatives are a bar and positioning question.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $4.12. Sources: ChartRow, 8 estimates, as of the 2026-10-09 close (https://chartrow.com/quote/unh/earnings); IG preview of 2026-10-06, $4.12 on revenue of $111.38B (https://www.ig.com/en-ch/news-and-trade-ideas/unitedhealth-stock-q3-2026-earnings-preview-261006); TipRanks of 2026-10-12, $4.14 (https://www.tipranks.com/news/unitedhealth-q3-earnings-tomorrow-3-make-or-break-factors-for-unh-stock). The two estimate sources agree. Q3 MCR consensus is 90.1% (TipRanks, single source). The company guide: FY26 adjusted EPS $19.50-20.00, MCR 88.1% +/-25bp (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000191/earningsrelease2q26_7152.htm). H1 adjusted EPS was $13.61, so the guide implies H2 of $5.89-6.39, and the company said 'slightly more earnings in 3Q relative to 4Q', which puts guide-implied Q3 at about $3.0-3.4. FY26 consensus was $19.81 and FY27 $22.44 as of 2026-09-09 (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/09/unitedhealth-slips-3-as-tpg-buys-into-florida-wellmed-clinics-ahead-of-guidance-reaffirmation/).
positioning_check: Short interest is about 15.1M shares, ~1.7% of float, ~2.5 days to cover, per Equibles' 2026-08-19 snapshot, down ~13% m/m (https://equibles.com/stocks/UNH). It was 17.3M / 3.5 DTC on 2026-07-15 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/unh/short-interest/). Not crowded. Baseline 25-delta skew is -7.2 vol points, so upside is paid, with put/call OI 1.23 and an event-implied move of 6.57%. Spot $375.29 is -14% from the 52-week high (~$461, touched after the July print), with a 20-day run-up of -2.15% and 5-day of -0.87%. Sell-side is Strong Buy (17 Buy / 4 Hold) with an average target of about $485, so consensus is long and positioned for a beat.

findings.finding: At the Wells Fargo conference on 2026-09-09, CFO Wayne DeVeydt said the medical-cost improvement behind the Q2 beat continued through July-August ('that durability has not dissipated'). He also said MA margins are tracking the upper half of the 2-4% range and Optum Health will reach a 2% margin this year, ahead of prior expectations. Against the guide-implied Q3 MCR (about 90-91% for H2 on an 88.1% FY guide with H1 near 85.3%) and the 90.1% consensus, this points to a Q3 MCR at or below consensus and a likely third FY raise above $19.50-20.00.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 MCR beat plus raise: +6.96% (baseline). Q2 2026 MCR beat ($6.38 vs ~$4.9) plus raise to $19.50-20.00: +7.3% pre-market faded to +1.16% close (baseline), then -18% over the next three months. The same line has paid once fully and once barely.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. Q3 consensus rose from $3.66 (Zacks, 2026-07-30) to $4.12, about $0.8 above the guide's own cadence, so the street has already moved for it. If it were fully priced, the stock would not sit 18% below the post-Q2 high on flat estimates. The residual is the size of the FY raise and of the MCR beat beyond 90.1%, which the CFO did not quantify.
findings.independence: TD Cowen (Ryan Langston) models Optum Health Q3 operating earnings of $299M against management's ~$150M (https://www.tipranks.com/news/unitedhealth-q3-earnings-tomorrow-3-make-or-break-factors-for-unh-stock, 2026-10-12). HCA's July guide cut on weak outpatient surgery (finding 6) is a counterparty pointing the same way. Hudson Labs' preview (2026-09-28) restates MA above 3% (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/unitedhealth-q3-2026-earnings-preview-unh-guidance-margins), but that rests on the same company statements.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the company guided a 'two-thirds, one-third first half to back half mix' with 'slightly more earnings in 3Q relative to 4Q'. On H1 adjusted EPS of $13.61 and an FY guide of $19.50-20.00, that implies Q3 of about $3.0-3.4. The $4.12 consensus therefore already requires Q3 to beat the company's own cadence by ~$0.7-1.1 (20-35%). A Q3 that beats the guide's cadence but lands below $4.12 would headline as a miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two quarters beat consensus by ~10% (Q1, $7.23 vs ~$6.6) and ~30% (Q2, $6.38 vs ~$4.9) while the guide sat far below. Management has consistently printed above both cadence and street this year, so this bar risk has not materialised in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews quote $4.12 against last year's $2.92 and do not reconcile it with the company's H2 cadence. If the market were anchoring on the guide-implied ~$3.2, consensus would sit near that, as Zacks' $3.66 in July roughly did. The $4.12 bar means the street expects a beat versus the guide, so the risk is that the beat is smaller than the street has built in.
findings.independence: The arithmetic uses the H1 EPS in the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000731766/000073176626000191/earningsrelease2q26_7152.htm). Zacks' July estimates of Q3 $3.66 / Q4 $2.25 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/zacks-research-issues-positive-forecast-for-unh-earnings-2026-07-31/) were consistent with the guide before consensus rose. It shares no source with finding 1 but bears on the same print: finding 1 says the trend is better than plan, this says the bar has already moved for it.

findings.finding: The Q3 call is the first likely look at 2027. The CFO has publicly set Optum Health margin at 4% in 2027 (from ~2% in 2026), Medicaid back toward breakeven (from -1% to -1.7%), and MA 'positioned for stability' in the upper half of 2-4%. On ~$94B of Optum Health revenue, +2pts is about +$1.9B pre-tax, or ~+$1.6/share. Together with Medicaid that supports the $22.44 FY27 consensus (+13%), even though commercial recovery is pushed beyond 2027 and 2026 carries $860M of PPD and a light flu season.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward-year guide reactions are the large moves on this name: the January 2026 2026 guide plus MA rate shock was -19.6%, and the April 2025 guide cut was -22.4% (baseline). The Q3 2025 print, with a first 2026 growth view, was +0.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: At $375 the stock is ~16.7x the $22.44 FY27 consensus and 18% below the July high. If the market believed $22.44, the multiple would not sit at what TIKR calls a trough of ~18x forward. The discount looks like doubt about 2027 (2.48% MA final rate, 15% stars decline, sticky commercial trend), which a confirming 2027 view would address. The size of the 2027 view is inference from company targets, not a disclosed number.
findings.independence: Hudson Labs preview (2026-09-28) lists the same 2027 segment targets from company statements (https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/unitedhealth-q3-2026-earnings-preview-unh-guidance-margins), so it is not independent. Elevance reaffirmed at least 12% 2027 EPS growth in June (https://quartr.com/events/elevance-health-inc-elv-goldman-sachs-47th-annual-global-healthcare-conference-2026_3e3sMZqa), a peer pointing to sector 2027 recovery.

findings.finding: KFF's 2027 plan landscape (2026-10-09) shows UnitedHealth exiting 228 counties and entering 9, so it offers MA-PDs in ~70% of counties against ~80% in 2026. The preliminary list shared with brokers in August named 34 counties and ~20,000 members. That points to a larger 2027 MA membership and revenue decline than the August list suggested, after ~1.1M members lost in 2026. It is margin-accretive but a revenue headwind for the 2027 view.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2026 the market rewarded margin over membership: the MA retreat and ~1.1M member loss came with the Q1/Q2 beat-and-raises (+6.96%, +1.16%). The January 2026 revenue-decline guide was part of the -19.6% day.
findings.why_not_priced: Published two sessions before the print, and the stock was flat over 5 days (-0.87%), so it has had little time to be digested. The membership consequence is not quantified until management gives a 2027 MA enrollment view. If priced as a negative, the stock would have dropped on 10-09.
findings.independence: The 34-county preliminary list (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/unitedhealthcare-medicare-advantage-2027-market-competitive/829889/) is the contrast. Budget Seniors (2026-10-06) reports plans covering 390,000 members shut for 2027 (https://www.budgetseniors.com/?p=6344), a less established source. ConsumerAffairs cites ~140 counties. The sources disagree on scale.

findings.finding: In CMS's 2027 Star Ratings released 2026-10-08, UnitedHealth's average rating fell ~15% (Oppenheimer), against Humana's rise to ~95% of members in 4+ star plans. UNH said the results were in line with its expectations, and shares fell ~0.5% in extended trading. The ratings drive 2028 quality bonus payments, so the effect for this print is only through call commentary on 2028 and the competitive position.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the September 2025 preliminary stars update (78% in 4+) UNH rose ~9% in a session. On this release it fell 0.5% after hours. Stars news has moved this name before but did not on 10-08.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock barely moved, and the company called it expected. The residual is whether management quantifies the 2028 bonus hit on the call, which no one has sized publicly.
findings.independence: Healthcare Dive 2026-10-09 reports UNH and CVS with 'double-digit percentage reductions' in 4+ star membership (https://healthcaredive.com/news/medicare-advantage-stars-2027-winners-losers/832582).

findings.finding: HCA, the largest US hospital counterparty, cut its 2026 net income outlook in July to $6.3-6.7B. Q2 outpatient surgeries fell 4.4% consolidated (3.4% same-facility) and admissions grew 2.5%, so provider volumes were softening going into Q3. That is consistent with payer cost trend below plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history. Payer prints have tracked provider volume commentary loosely.
findings.source_date: 2026-07 (HCA Q2 2026 results; URL undated, content references Q2 2026 and the 10-Q for 2026-06-30)
findings.why_not_priced: It is old (July), and UNH raised its guide after seeing the same quarter. It is a proxy for July-September utilization, not a Q3 company number, so it carries little that is new.
findings.independence: HCA 10-Q for 2026-06-30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000860730/000119312526321077/hca-20260630.htm). This is a proxy and does not confirm UNH's Q3 directly.

findings.finding: No managed-care peer pre-announced a Q3 problem. Centene reaffirmed adjusted EPS >$4.80 on 2026-08-17 and again in its Deutsche Bank conference 8-K of 2026-09-16 (valid through 09-25). This contrasts with July 2025, when a peer guidance withdrawal preceded UNH's sector-wide reset.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer guidance withdrawals in 2025 preceded UNH's -7.5% (2025-07-29) print. Their absence this quarter removes that setup.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced as an absence of bad news. It is filed because it removes a known negative route into the print rather than adding a positive.
findings.independence: Centene 8-K 2026-08-17 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001071739/000107173926000165/a20260817formex991pressrel.htm). Humana reaffirmed at least $9.00 (https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/humana-hum-reaffirms-fy26-adj-eps-guidance-of-at-least-usd-900, undated).

findings.finding: Positioning leans long into the print. The skew is -7.2 (calls bid over puts), the sell-side is 17 Buy / 4 Hold with an average target of ~$485 (+28%), short interest is ~1.7% of float, and Q3 consensus has already risen from $3.66 to $4.12. On the last beat-and-raise (Q2, $6.38 vs ~$4.9, guide up to $19.50-20.00) the stock went +7.3% pre-market, closed only +1.16%, then fell 18% over three months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a large beat plus raise gave +1.16% close (baseline). Q3 2025: a modest beat gave +0.51%. Q1 2026: beat plus raise gave +6.96%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: upside skew and a raised bar mean a good print is expected. Any residual is in how the session handles a beat. Pre-market strength faded last time, and the window is close to close.
findings.independence: The baseline's skew -7.2 and put/call OI 1.23 are sealed. The TipRanks preview of 2026-10-12 gives the Strong Buy consensus and $485 target (https://www.tipranks.com/news/unitedhealth-q3-earnings-tomorrow-3-make-or-break-factors-for-unh-stock).

findings.finding: Capital return was stepped up: at least $5.0B of 2026 buybacks against an initial $2.5B, $4.0B done by mid-July, operating cash flow guide ~$24B (from >$18B), and debt/capital 41.2% against a ~40% year-end target. That leaves room for an increased buyback or a 2027 capital-return figure on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. Buyback increases came bundled with the Q1/Q2 raises.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. Only a fresh increase would be new, and none has been signalled.
findings.independence: TIKR 2026-09-11 says buybacks roughly doubled (https://www.tikr.com/blog/unitedhealths-cfo-says-the-cost-trend-held-into-q3-heres-what-the-turnaround-could-be-worth), but that rests on the same company statement.

outside_window.finding: Humana's 2027 stars at ~95% of members in 4+ plans (Oppenheimer estimates +$3.6B of revenue) against UNH's ~15% average decline gives Humana a 2028 bonus-funded benefit advantage in MA competition. The economic effect falls in the 2028 plan year.
The 2027 MA open-enrollment outcome (2026-10-15 to 12-07) after exits from 228 counties. It decides actual 2027 MA membership and is only visible in January 2027.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the skew, which pays for upside, and with the street's raised bar. So the positive company-level facts are largely priced, and the residual lean is small. The -2.15% 20-day run-up and the 18% drawdown from the July high are the only things leaving room for a positive reaction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1, reaction function: the Q2 beat-and-raise faded from +7.3% pre-market to +1.16% close, so finding 1 (Q3 cost durability) was cut from +1.0 to +0.8.

Lesson 5, documents beat inference: finding 3 (the 2027 view) is arithmetic built from company targets, not a disclosed number, so it was cut from +0.8 to +0.6. Finding 6 (the HCA proxy) was cut from +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 7, positioning: the positive lean agrees with an upside-paid skew of -7.2, so p_up moved from 54 to 53 and the scaled move from +0.56 to +0.42.

Lesson 6, verify the bar: the $4.12 bar was confirmed by two agreeing sources (ChartRow 8 estimates, IG) plus TipRanks $4.14, so no cap was applied. Finding 2 is kept: the bar sits outside the company's own guide cadence.

Lesson 3, read the set: findings 1 and 2 bear on the same print from different documents (the trend is better than plan versus a bar already raised for it). They are not contradictory and are kept with opposite signs.
